comparisons.peer_summary: AMD's AI strategy is focused on three priorities: delivering a broad portfolio of high-performance adaptive hardware and software solutions, expanding ecosystem partnerships to accelerate deployments, and providing compelling user experiences via the open ROCm software platform.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and AMD frame their corporate strategy around a comprehensive approach to AI infrastructure and software, specifically highlighting open platforms and ecosystem partnerships. Intel explicitly states its strategy involves 'open and modular solutions' for 'competitive total cost of ownership' to support the full AI continuum. Similarly, AMD defines its strategy around 'delivering a broad portfolio... and expanding ecosystem partnerships' to accelerate deployments via an 'open and proven software platform' (ROCm). While Intel focuses on the 'full spectrum' of hardware/software for the entire continuum, AMD emphasizes the 'open' nature of its software to enable broad deployment across its adaptive hardware.

sentences.text: We believe we have a full spectrum of hardware and software platforms that offer the open and modular solutions for competitive total cost of ownership and time to value that customers need to win in this era of exponential growth and AI everywhere.
Our strategy is to bring AI to where the data is being generated and used.
The second is expanding the deep and collaborative partnerships we have established across the ecosystem to accelerate deployments of AMD based AI solutions at scale.
And the third is providing compelling user experiences to extend the open and proven software platform we have established that enables our AI hardware to be deployed more broadly and easily.

comparisons.peer_summary: AMD was the first company to integrate a dedicated neural processing unit (NPU) on the same SoC as an x86 CPU for AI PCs.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies identify 'AI PCs' as a key emerging usage within the broader AI continuum. Intel includes 'AI PCs' as part of its strategy to address every phase from GenAI to the edge, leveraging its full spectrum of technologies. AMD highlights a specific competitive milestone: being the 'first company to integrate a dedicated neural processing unit (NPU) on the same SoC as an x86 CPU for AI PCs.' Intel’s comparison is broader, covering the entire continuum including edge and cloud, whereas AMD’s submission is narrowly focused on the hardware differentiation in the client PC segment.

sentences.text: We also seek to address every phase of the AI continuum, from the largest, most challenging GenAI and large language models to emerging usages like AI PCs and AI at the edge.

We are infusing AI into Intel technologies, supporting today's GenAI workloads, fueling emerging usages like AI PC and AI at the edge, and pioneering innovations that we believe will help advance the future of AI in the next decade.
AMD was the first company to integrate a dedicated neural processing unit (NPU) on the same SoC as an x86 CPU for AI PCs.

comparisons.peer_summary: The company offers infrastructure and security software to simplify IT environments, support hybrid cloud platforms, and manage mission-critical workloads for Fortune 500 companies and government agencies, including fibre channel storage networking products.
comparisons.comparison: While Intel emphasizes 'open and modular solutions' for AI everywhere, Avago (Broadcom) focuses on infrastructure software to manage and secure the environments where AI data centers reside. Both address the 'data center' and 'edge' computing needs. Intel’s strategy is to 'bring AI to where the data is being generated and used' using hardware/software platforms. Avago’s submission details how its software helps enterprises 'manage and secure their on-premises and hybrid cloud environments, private cloud infrastructure and AI data centers,' noting that customers use these solutions to 'plan, develop, deliver, automate, manage, and secure applications.' Intel provides the AI computing fabric; Avago provides the management software for the underlying infrastructure.

sentences.text: Our strategy is to bring AI to where the data is being generated and used.

We believe we have a full spectrum of hardware and software platforms that offer the open and modular solutions for competitive total cost of ownership and time to value that customers need to win in this era of exponential growth and AI everywhere.

Our infrastructure software solutions help enterprises simplify their information technology ("IT") environments so they can increase business velocity and flexibility, and enable customers to plan, develop, deliver, automate, manage, and secure applications across mainframe, distributed, edge, mobile, and private and hybrid cloud platforms.

Many of the largest companies in the world, including most of the Fortune 500, and many government agencies rely on our software solutions to help manage and secure their on-premises and hybrid cloud environments, private cloud infrastructure and AI data centers.

comparisons.peer_summary: Next-generation PCs feature AI capabilities and high-performance neural processing chipsets, leading to significantly higher DRAM content, with the company announcing low-power compression-attached memory modules to support AI workloads on PCs.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and Micron explicitly identify 'AI PCs' as a major market driver characterized by increased hardware requirements. Micron provides specific technical context for this trend, noting that 'next generation PCs... contain high-performance neural processing chipsets as well as AI' and will have 'significantly more DRAM content than today's average PC.' Both disclosures link the rise of AI PCs directly to hardware innovation and component demand.

comparisons.peer_summary: Demand for AI and big data is driving the need for high-performance storage; SBU addresses this with the 6500 30TB SSD for AI data lakes and sampled the 9550 series in 2024 for AI and high-performance computing workloads.

comparisons.peer_summary: NVIDIA has evolved from pioneering accelerated computing to becoming a full-stack computing infrastructure company with data-center-scale offerings that reshape industry.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and NVIDIA describe a strategic evolution towards becoming comprehensive computing infrastructure leaders. Intel states it has a 'full spectrum of hardware and software platforms' and views AI as a 'generational shift in computing.' NVIDIA describes its evolution from 'pioneered accelerated computing' to becoming a 'full-stack computing infrastructure company with data-center-scale offerings.' Both peers position themselves as providers of the foundational compute infrastructure necessary for the 'exponential growth' and 'challenging problems' driven by AI, though Intel emphasizes modularity and open solutions while NVIDIA emphasizes its full-stack proprietary advantage.

sentences.text: We believe AI represents a generational shift in computing by expanding human abilities and solving the most challenging problems.

comparisons.peer_summary: NVIDIA leverages its AI technology leadership to deliver end-to-end automated driving and in-vehicle cockpit computing solutions under the DRIVE Hyperion brand, which includes high-performance computing hardware, sensor sets, and software platforms for autonomous driving and intelligent in-vehicle experiences.

comparisons.peer_summary: Mobile handsets and PCs are becoming pervasive AI platforms with complex large generative AI algorithms running on-device to enable on-demand use cases at lower energy costs.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and Qualcomm explicitly identify 'AI PCs' as a key area of focus and growth. Intel states its strategy involves supporting 'emerging usages like AI PC' and addressing the 'AI continuum.' Qualcomm mirrors this by describing how 'mobile handsets and PCs are becoming pervasive AI platforms' with complex generative AI algorithms running on-device. Both recognize the shift of AI workloads to client devices, emphasizing low energy costs and on-device processing, with Intel framing it as part of its broader portfolio strategy and Qualcomm detailing the specific on-device capability trends.

sentences.text: We also seek to address every phase of the AI continuum, from the largest, most challenging GenAI and large language models to emerging usages like AI PCs and AI at the edge.

With increased processing power, mobile handsets and PCs are becoming pervasive AI platforms, with complex large generative AI algorithms running on-device, enabling on-demand and contextual AI use cases at a fraction of the energy required by cloud-based applications.

As wireless connectivity complements on-device generative AI, edge devices enable enhanced productivity use cases, while intelligently processing and sharing data with cloud-based applications as needed.

comparisons.peer_topic: Processor architecture and AI Engine capabilities
comparisons.peer_summary: Qualcomm utilizes System-on-Chip architecture with heterogeneous computing, including Oryon and Kryo CPUs and Adreno GPUs, to enable high-performance, low-power computing. The Qualcomm AI Engine features dedicated hardware and the Hexagon NPU for high-performance on-device AI inference, supported by the AI Stack and AI Hub to simplify developer integration.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and Qualcomm discuss the hardware architecture enabling on-device AI. Intel claims a 'full spectrum of hardware... platforms' to support AI workloads. Qualcomm details its 'System-on-Chip architecture' and 'Qualcomm AI Engine' with a dedicated 'Hexagon NPU' for 'sustained, high-performance AI inference' with 'very low power consumption.' While Intel speaks generally about its hardware spectrum and software integration, Qualcomm provides specific architectural details (NPU, Kryo/Oryon CPUs) that support the 'AI PC' and edge device strategies both companies advocate.

sentences.text: We believe we have a full spectrum of hardware and software platforms that offer the open and modular solutions for competitive total cost of ownership and time to value that customers need to win in this era of exponential growth and AI everywhere.

We are infusing AI into Intel technologies, supporting today's GenAI workloads, fueling emerging usages like AI PC and AI at the edge, and pioneering innovations that we believe will help advance the future of AI in the next decade.

The Qualcomm® AI Engine, featured in our Snapdragon platforms and many of our other products, includes dedicated hardware capable of running complex AI use cases at high-performance and low-power on device, while also enhancing privacy and security.

Our Qualcomm® Hexagon™ NPU is a key processor in our AI Engine and is designed for sustained, high-performance AI inference, enabling leading on-device AI capabilities with very low power consumption.
